newsitem.title: JAPAN: Nikkei loses 345 points as blue-chip boom slows.
newsitem.headline: Nikkei loses 345 points as blue-chip boom slows.

text.p: The Tokyo stock market's key Nikkei 225 average tumbled on Monday as a recent boom in blue-chip issues slowed, driving dealers to unload long positions. Brokers expected the Nikkei to seek the bottom of recent range-bound trading.
The Nikkei 225 ended down 345.67 points or 1.64 percent at 20,674.69. Its December futures were 420 lower at 20,680.
"The Nikkei average is likely to gauge the bottom of the recent range this week, after it tested the upper side last week," said Tetsuya Ishijima, chief strategist Okasan Securities Co Ltd.
"The focus is on whether it will be supported at around 20,500," he said.
The recent rally in blue-chip issues had been led by foreign investors' aggressive buying, backed by the global firms' solid half-year earnings announced mainly in November.
But the lack of any fresh impetus took away support for the buying, brokers said.
Turnover was a thin 224 million shares on Monday, down from Friday's 292 million shares.
Declining issues beat advancing ones 856 to 225, while 171 issues were unchanged.
The broader TOPIX index also dropped 20.61 points or 1.32 percent to end at 1,542.19, while the Nikkei 300 average was 4.31 points or 1.46 percent lower at 291.25.

The market has been recently split into winning sectors such as automobiles and electronics, which have continued to set record highs, and weak sectors which have kept slipping to their year's lows, brokers said.
"In that situation, new sectors have not appeared to support the buying trend," Ishijima said.
Brokers said that loss-cutting sales by dealers accelerated after the Nikkei average fell below 21,000.
Trading was mostly subdued until shortly before the close, when the sell-off took hold, they said.
Market attention was on shares in Nippon Broadcasting System Inc, which were listed on the second section of the Tokyo Stock Exchange on Monday, brokers said.
The share price of the major Japanese broadcasting firm was bid-only at 7,550 yen at the end of the session.
"The heavy buying orders highlight the market's belief that the outlook for the firm is bright," said Kenichi Sagami, general manager at Yamaichi Securities Co Ltd.
Shares in Nippon Telegraph and Telephone Corp (NTT) first jumped as investors reacted positively to a newspaper report on its possible reorganisation, but fell back slightly.
The share price of the Japanese telecommunications giant finished 1,000 yen lower at 811,000 yen.

The Japanese business daily Nihon Keizai Shimbun said on Monday that the Ministry of Posts and Telecommunications and NTT had reached an agreement on a new structure for the firm as early as the 1998/99 business year.

An NTT spokesman said an agreement was expected to be reached this month. An official at the posts ministry said the ministry was seeking to conclude an agreement as soon as possible on breaking up NTT.
The second section index fell 13.08 points to close at 1,944.07, with 9.17 million shares traded.
The over-the-counter (OTC) index was down 14.29 points at 1,381.89.
-- Hiroko Nakata, Tokyo Equities Desk +81-3-3432-8027
